newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Privatised Ivorian telecom firm gets 7 yr monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Privatised Ivorian telecom firm gets 7 yr monopoly.

text.p: Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie has signed a decree giving the new owners of the privatised state telecommunications firm CI-TELCOM a seven-year monopoly.

A government statement, read on state television after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, said the measure was designed to ensure the success of the privatised company in which a consortium led by France Telecom has a 51 percent stake.
"This concession is valid for 20 years with an exclusive period of seven years for exclusive services," the statement said.

Privatisation of CI-TELCOM was the jewel in the crown of the West African nation's privatisation programme. France Telecom will pay the state around $190 million cash for its ceding last week of a 51 percent stake in the company.
A total of 37 of the 60 companies earmarked for privatisation have been sold partly or in full to the private sector.
Ivory Coast has been privatising state companies as part of reforms sponsored by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund to liberalise its economy.

Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan told a privatisation open day on Wednesday that the government has earned about 100 billion CFA francs ($181.8 million) from the sale of state enterprises up to the end of last December.
The figure did not inclue the CI-TELCOM sale.
